target_customer: B2B SaaS and enterprise security teams that must answer customer security reviews and questionnaires
problem: Security teams spent large amounts of time answering repeat vendor security questionnaires and document requests from customers. A shared Trust Center let buyers self serve that information.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription for the Trust Center platform, priced by company
product_category: Trust management and security review automation

founders.name: Al Yang
founders.background_notes: Per YC profile, started SafeBase to help companies share their security and compliance posture.

founders.name: Adar Arnon
founders.background_notes: Former R&D group leader in an elite IDF technology unit, specializing in cybersecurity and OS architecture.

technical_complexity.rationale: Core Trust Center is a gated document and content portal with integrations, standard SaaS engineering. Questionnaire automation added later needed more AI work.

defensibility.rationale: Customers integrate the trust center into sales and security workflows, and buyers get used to the format, but the product was copyable by compliance platforms, which is how Drata and Vanta later competed.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Compliance platforms later added trust center features. Drata acquired SafeBase in February 2025 and unified the brand into Drata in March 2026.

market_need_then: Enterprise buyers sent long vendor security questionnaires and SaaS sellers answered them repeatedly. SafeBase later reported over 700 customers by April 2024 and over 1,000 at the acquisition, which shows demand grew.

branding.domain_note: Used safebase.io, which now redirects to drata.com.
branding.brand_signature: The Trust Center as a product category name, with branded Trust Center pages carrying the SafeBase name

rebrands.why: Drata consolidated the acquired SafeBase brand into the single Drata name after the 2025 acquisition

branding.community_and_virality: RSA Innovation Sandbox finalist and Fortune Cyber60 listing per Series B coverage; customer trust pages exposed the brand widely, reported at over two million views.

brand_strength.rationale: Recognized by security teams and showcased with logos such as OpenAI and LinkedIn, plus awards. The name is descriptive and there is no evidence of mascot or merch.

outcome_analysis: SafeBase built a Trust Center for security reviews, raised an 18 million dollar Series A in 2022 led by NEA and a 33 million dollar Series B in 2024 led by Touring Capital, and grew to over 700 customers with 98 percent retention before Drata agreed to buy it in February 2025. The price was not disclosed by the companies, and the brand was folded into Drata in 2026.
notes: SecurityWeek reported a 250M dollar deal value that the companies did not confirm, so amount is null. No seed round amount found, so the history is partial. No competitor sources dated near mid 2020 were found; search returned only 2025 vendor comparison pages naming Whistic, Vanta, OneTrust and Conveyor, which are not used. Name origin and logo not found.
